name: Arin
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Extinct 18th-c. Yeniseian known only from wordlists; Wikipedia phonology page has no stress statement and no stress-bearing source.

sources.citation: Khabtagaeva, Bayarma. 2019. Language Contact in Siberia: Turkic, Mongolic, and Tungusic Loanwords in Yeniseian (The Languages of Asia 19). Leiden/Boston: Brill.
sources.note: §3.3 'Arin' (p. 9): c. 400 items; grammatical sketch and lexicon in Werner 2005: 142-168; historical phonetics examined by Toporov 1968; archive material Helimski 1986. Stress remarks in the loanword analyses invoke 'Yeniseian stress on the first syllable' / 'the stress on the first syllable in the Yeniseian languages' to explain Kott vowel changes (e.g. pp. on Kott arak, askar, koŋar), and once 'possibly stressed' second syllable for an Assan form 'cf. Kott and Arin forms' -- no statement about where stress falls in Arin.

Vowel and consonant tables sourced to Werner 2005; note that [ʔ] 'is only assumed from other Yeniseian languages and is only a prosodic device of tone'. No stress statement. Used for bibliography only.

sources.citation: Bonmann, Svenja & Simon Fries. 2025. Linguistic Evidence Suggests that Xiōng-nú and Huns Spoke the Same Paleo-Siberian Language. Transactions of the Philological Society (early view), 1-24. doi:10.1111/1467-968X.12321 (CC-BY 4.0).
sources.note: Treats (Old) Arin segmental correspondences; the only prosodic content is a footnote on Ket/Yugh tone notation (Vajda 2004, Georg 2007). Nothing on Arin stress or accent.

sources.citation: Гришина Н. М. 2009. Аринский язык // Историческая энциклопедия Сибири: в 3 т. Новосибирск: Историческое наследие Сибири (Irkipedia transcription, Internet Archive copy 2018-11-25).
sources.note: One-paragraph phonology after Toporov 1968: 'Его звуковая система, по данным В.Н. Топорова, характеризуется, по-видимому, противопоставлением заднеязычных увулярным (и фарингальным).. а также отсутствием противопоставления по твердости-мягкости на фонологическом уровне.' Silent on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Georg, Stefan. 2007. A Descriptive Grammar of Ket (Yenisei-Ostyak). Part 1. Folkestone: Global Oriental. §2.2.4 'Arin', p. 18.
sources.note: Arin: c. 400 lexical items from Strahlenberg, Müller, Fischer (via Klaproth, Pallas); 'All available Arin data from earlier sources have been collected and analyzed by Toporov (1968)', plus Chelimskij 1986 archive list. Nothing on Arin prosody.

sources.citation: Werner, Heinrich. 2002. Vergleichendes Wörterbuch der Jenissej-Sprachen. Bd. 1-3. Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz.
sources.note: Vorbemerkungen and 'Orthographie und Transkription' read. Tone numbers are written before the syllable and are 'gleichzeitig ein Hinweis auf die Betonung der folgenden Silbe' (applies to Ket/Yugh field data). The c. 610 Arin ('ar.') citations are 18th-century spellings (Müller, Fischer, Strahlenberg, Helimski archive) without accent marks; no per-language phonology section; nothing on Arin stress.

sources.citation: Вернер Г. К. 1997. Енисейские языки // Языки мира: Палеоазиатские языки (ред. А. П. Володин и др.). Москва: Индрик, с. 169-177.
sources.note: Family article. Section 6 'Фонетика' (pp. 172-173) gives only a family-wide remark: ablaut and four vowel heights 'исторически связаны со слоговой акцентуацией (слоговыми тонами), которая резко отличает Е.я. от окружающих'; tone oppositions exemplified from Ket/Yugh only. Arin appears only in classification (арино-пумпокольская группа, phonetic isoglosses k-/h- retention, syncope, vowel correspondences, p. 171) and hydronyms. No statement on Arin word stress.

sources.citation: Vajda, Edward. 2024. The Yeniseian language family. In E. Vajda (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of Northern Asia, 365-480. Berlin/Boston: De Gruyter Mouton.
